entrypoints.summary: Inputs reaching Fr::from_repr() conversion sites, including Winning PoSt or Window PoSt randomness and similarly prover_id; the report requires per-occurrence manual review to establish malicious-user reachability.

impacts.concept: proof generation and verification availability failure

mitigations.concept: validated byte provenance plus handled conversion errors

relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that Fr::from_repr() errors above the field modulus and that affected callers use unwrap(), expect(), or similarly panic-prone Result access.
The report identifies conversion-triggered panics and reports as_safe_commitment-related errors in PoSt generation and verification when randomness exceeds the modulus.

relation_candidates.dst: proof generation and verification availability failure
relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that proofs cannot be created when generated randomness is not below the field modulus and that generation and verification error.

relation_candidates.dst: validated byte provenance plus handled conversion errors
relation_candidates.rationale: The documented resolution distinguishes checked B[32]safe inputs, where conversion is guaranteed Ok, from unchecked B[32] inputs, where the error case is handled.

impact.affected_asset: Winning PoSt and Window PoSt proof generation and verification processing.
impact.attacker_capability: Conditionally cause field-conversion failure at a maliciously reachable unchecked conversion input; the report does not establish external reachability for every listed occurrence.
impact.security_effect: Proof-generation or proof-verification liveness/availability disruption through a conversion-triggered panic or returned error.

causal_trace.summary: A byte-like value supplied to Fr::from_repr() is greater than the field modulus, so it is not a canonical field representation.
A conversion path assumes a field representation is valid despite accepting an unchecked value; Fr::from_repr() instead returns an error for the out-of-modulus representation.

Affected locations access the conversion Result through unwrap(), expect(), or other panic-prone Result access, turning the conversion error into a panic; as_safe_commitment() makes out-of-range PoSt randomness cause generation and verification errors.

The documented effect is inability to create proofs for randomness outside the field modulus and errors in Winning/Window PoSt generation and verification; this is a proof-processing liveness/availability failure.

failure.operation: Unhandled Fr::from_repr() conversion error via panic-prone Result access (with reported PoSt generation/verification errors through as_safe_commitment())

primary_invariant.statement: Only checked byte arrays whose values are below the field modulus may enter an infallible field conversion; unchecked byte arrays must retain and handle the Fr::from_repr() error path.
primary_invariant.violated_because: An out-of-modulus input can reach Fr::from_repr(), which returns an error, while callers use unwrap(), expect(), or another panic-prone Result access.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report directly supports the field-modulus precondition, panic-prone Result handling, PoSt error behavior, and specification-level resolution. The bundle contains no audited source snapshot, call-site-specific public-API dataflow, patch commit, executable reproducer, or execution result. The report expressly says each occurrence must be manually reviewed for malicious-user reachability; remote or user-controlled triggering must therefore remain conditional.

remediation.invariant_restored: The resolution specifies B[32]safe for byte arrays checked such that from_repr() is guaranteed Result::Ok(), while ordinary unchecked B[32] inputs use a path that handles the conversion error.

target.component: Multiple byte-to-field conversion and PoSt processing locations
